title: Tessera Bank workload model
description: The shape of one business day of demand, declared as a contract so that every driver that executes it - WP-21 against the modern spine, WP-25 against the older strata - is executing the same day. The model performs no I/O and names no host: it states what customers do and when, never where the request goes. Every time in this document is local civil time at the bank; mapping a minute of the day onto an instant is the driver's job, not the model's.

modelId.description: Format identifier. A driver that does not recognise it must refuse the model rather than guess at it.

modelVersion.description: Semantic version of this model instance. The run manifest records the digest as well, because a version somebody forgot to raise is the failure this guards against.

summary.description: Prose. What bank, and what day, this model claims to describe.

realTime.description: What this model asks for in real time, at scale 1.0 and compression 1. A run at any other setting states both dials in its manifest, so that nothing claims a throughput a run did not produce.

dailyEventCount.description: Events across an ordinary weekday with every calendar multiplier at 1.0. Cross-checked against the population: the cohorts and their per-customer rates have to add up to this number.

peakToTroughRatio.description: The busiest hour of the diurnal curve divided by the quietest. Declared here and asserted against the curve, because a flat rate with a nice name is the thing this model exists not to be.

calendar.description: When demand happens. The diurnal curve is a shape rather than a rate - the engine normalises it so that a day's total is dailyEventCount - and the multipliers below scale the whole day.

diurnal.description: Relative intensity by hour of local civil time, index 0 being 00:00. Shape only; the absolute rate comes from realTime.dailyEventCount.

weekday.description: Whole-day multiplier by day of week. A Saturday is not a Tuesday with fewer people awake; it is a different day.

payday.description: Salary dates. Compounds with monthEnd when a date falls in both.

monthEnd.description: The closing days of the month, counted back from the last. Compounds with payday.

windows.description: Named spans of the day a driver needs to know about. A window whose endMinute is not after its startMinute wraps midnight.

population.description: Who generates the demand. References only - there is no field in this model a person's name, address or identifier could be written into, and the checker refuses a schema that grows one.

size.description: Distinct synthetic customers. The gateway limits per token subject plus route class (ADR 0006), so a population of thousands is what makes meaningful load possible as well as what makes it realistic.

share.description: Fraction of the population. The shares add to 1 and each must yield a whole number of customers.

currencyMix.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic codes to weights adding to 1.

operationMix.description: OpenAPI operationId to weight, adding to 1. Every key must be an operationId the ledger actually serves; the checker reads them from contracts/openapi/ledger-core.yaml rather than from a list copied into it.

amountDistribution.description: Log-normal in shape, stated in minor units and drawn as int64. There is no scale here and no decimal point: the currency's scale resolves the figure, per the canonical data model.
